content.text:
I read every input file, the full draft, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure and the affirmative USER passages.

**What traced cleanly**

- Claims 1–20: every limitation traces to the disclosure (rigid base with first/second sides; motor on the first side; extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber; rigid low-friction loop/skirt at the perimeter; no airtight seal; air entering beneath the perimeter; continuous extraction holding the chamber below atmospheric; pressure differential holding without operator downforce; rigid-component transmission with substantially less damping; free sliding across areas; handles for guiding; rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control). Claims 10, and the FIG. 6 / Field / Summary autonomous-mode matter, trace to the one affirmative USER disclosure message ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"). The purely operational "resume / rerun every gate" USER turns were treated as non-disclosure.
- All 17 numerals: each means one thing, each appears in at least one brief, each brief's bullet list matches its declared numeral list (FIG. 1: 7/7, FIG. 2: 6/6, FIG. 3: 2/2, FIG. 4: 7/7, FIG. 5: 3/3, FIG. 6: 2/2), and every in-text figure cross-reference points at a sheet that actually carries the numeral.
- Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are identical in FIG. 3 (source view), in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view lines, and in the Brief Description.
- Drawing conventions (rectangular slab, closed-loop frame, generic blocks, flat bearing-face end, schematic port gap) stay confined to the briefs with explicit disclaimers; the words "rectangular", "by way of example", and "any closed outline" appear nowhere in the application text, and 07-drawings verbalizes no shape, taper, depth, or contact topology for the bearing face, clearance, or port.
- No drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains in any section body.

**What I flagged:** one item — the abstract's absolute "little damping", where both the inventor and the rest of the application state only the comparative ("substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup").

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-20 (device, system, method), all 17 entries in the numeral table, all six figure briefs and their bullet/numeral lists, the Brief Description of the Drawings, and every structure, relationship, result, material, position, connection, operating condition and variant in the Field, Background, Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract were checked against the disclosure and against the affirmative USER passages in the conversation. The only affirmative USER disclosure turn ("I want to also add autonomous mode... we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion") supports the stirring-element embodiment, claim 10, the Field's "autonomously moving", the Summary's further embodiment, and FIG. 6; the remaining USER turns are operational resume/gate instructions and were not treated as technical support. Cross-checks performed: numeral-to-part uniqueness (each of 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48 denotes exactly one part and each appears on at least one sheet); brief bullet counts against declared numeral lists (FIG. 1 7/7, FIG. 2 6/6, FIG. 3 2/2, FIG. 4 7/7, FIG. 5 3/3, FIG. 6 2/2); section-designation identity for lines 2-2 and 4-4 across the FIG. 3 source-view brief, the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view statements, and 07-drawings; claim-to-description term identity for base/first side/second side/chamber/perimeter member/bearing face/clearance/exposed face/volumetric extraction rate/vibration transmission path; and claim antecedent basis. Depiction conventions (rectangular slab and ring, generic blocks for motor, handle, pump and stirring elements, the flat lower end of the perimeter member, the schematic through-gap for fluid communication, the schematic cord attachment) are each disclaimed inside their own brief, correspond to parts the inventor affirmatively disclosed, and are not verbalized in the application text: the words "rectangular", "by way of example" and "any closed outline" do not appear in any draft section, and 07-drawings recites no shape, taper, angle, depth, runout, or contact topology for the bearing face 26, the clearance 34, or the extraction port. No drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction, internal comment or unresolved alternative remains in any section body. One finding is reported: the Abstract asserts an absolute result ("vibration transfers with little damping") that neither the inventor nor any other passage of the application supports, the source and the remainder of the draft stating only the comparative "substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup"; a filing-clean replacement that also keeps the abstract inside the 150-word limit is given.

findings.title: Abstract states an absolute damping result ("little damping") that the inventor never asserts and that conflicts with the comparative statement used everywhere else in the application
findings.detail: The Abstract's closing sentence characterises the transfer in absolute terms: vibration transfers "with little damping". No affirmative inventor passage makes an absolute statement about the amount of damping. The disclosure states only a comparison against a flexible suction cup, and every other place in the application that states this result keeps that comparison (Summary: "the vibration crosses into the covering element with substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup"; Detailed Description, three times, e.g. "vibration passes from the base 12 into the perimeter member 24 with substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup"; claim 1 recites only rigidity of the path and interposes no performance figure). The absolute quantifier is therefore both untraced to the sources and internally inconsistent with the rest of the filing text. The nearest source passage shows the gap: the inventor's own sentence is comparative and contains no absolute measure. Note that the correction must be made without pushing the Abstract past the 150-word limit of 37 CFR 1.72(b); the Abstract is currently 145 words, so the substitution alone would leave 151 words and a compensating deletion is included in the fix.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/10-abstract.md): "Every member between the motor and the covering element is rigid, so vibration transfers with little damping, and the bearing face lets the device slide to successive areas without releasing the hold." Nearest inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "Because the vibration motor is connected to the tile through rigid components, vibration energy is transferred with substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup." No affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or in any USER turn of input/conversation.md states that the damping is little, small, negligible, or otherwise absolutely characterised.
findings.fix: In draft/10-abstract.md make two edits. (1) Replace "so vibration transfers with little damping" with "so vibration transfers with substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup". (2) In the third sentence, replace "a clearance remains against the exposed face of the covering element" with "a clearance remains against the exposed face". The Abstract then reads: "A vibration device for bedding covering elements into thinset, mortar or adhesive has a rigid base carrying a vibration motor and an air-extraction mechanism on its first side and a chamber on its second side. A rigid perimeter member of low-friction material such as plastic or PTFE surrounds the chamber, its end face forming a bearing face. It is not a seal: a clearance remains against the exposed face, so ambient air enters the chamber continuously. Air is withdrawn fast enough to keep the chamber below atmospheric pressure while air keeps entering, and the pressure differential presses the device onto the covering element without downward force from the operator. Every member between the motor and the covering element is rigid, so vibration transfers with substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup, and the bearing face lets the device slide to successive areas without releasing the hold." (147 words, single paragraph, consistent with the Summary, the Detailed Description and the disclosure.)
